support.es: En Japón, normalmente hacemos una reverencia.

lexicalSense.contextualMeaning: please tell me all your names
lexicalSense.sourceSentence: What is your full name, with both family names?

support.ja: フルネームは何ですか？

lexicalSense.contextualMeaning: my father gave me my first family name
lexicalSense.sourceSentence: My second family name comes from my mum.

support.ja: 私の一つ目の名字は父から来ています。
support.es: Mi primer apellido viene de mi padre.

lexicalSense.contextualMeaning: at what hour does the fire night begin
lexicalSense.sourceSentence: What time does la Cremà start on 19 March?

support.ja: ラ・クレマは何時に始まりますか？

lexicalSense.contextualMeaning: tell me the reason you put it in a fire
lexicalSense.sourceSentence: It's so beautiful. Why do you burn it?

support.ja: なぜそれを燃やすのですか？

lexicalSense.contextualMeaning: what is the price to sleep here one night
lexicalSense.sourceSentence: Hello! How much is a bed for one night?

support.es: ¿Cuánto cuesta una cama por una noche?

lexicalSense.sourceSentence: Can I have a stamp, please? This is my first day.

support.ja: スタンプを押してもらえますか？

lexicalSense.contextualMeaning: how many kilometres is it from here to the city
lexicalSense.sourceSentence: How far is it to Santiago from here?

support.ja: サンティアゴまでどのくらいですか？

lxc_34930585fcfe52fa.text: In part one, we learned about the history, places and food of Spain.

lxc_bddfce963abbcacb.text: Then we will practise three real conversations.

lxc_4c9b34cf97000fe0.text: Today we will learn about kisses, names, a fire festival, islands and a long walk.

lxc_44b898df59b291cb.text: They also do it with someone new, like a friend of a friend.

lxc_8b69de13ef2397da.text: At work, more people now shake hands, especially at a first meeting.

lxc_bcc50757542c84d4.text: So a Spanish person may feel a little hurt if a visitor steps back.

lxc_761ec44f685d9f6c.text: When people in Spain meet, they often give dos besos.

lxc_32ef2c5d4910e1e9.text: Dos besos is Spanish for two kisses, one on each cheek.

lxc_497f548df69e3ef7.text: For Spanish people, the two kisses are a normal, warm hello, like a smile.

lxc_514d97004aefc9e8.text: People do it with friends and family.

lxc_5b700017f355aa97.text: If they are close friends or family, they often hug.

lxc_1834d8c7092c5959.text: People make a small kiss sound in the air.

lxc_abc51785ce913b9f.text: Women do this with women, and men do it with women.

lxc_963102ce081325b5.text: It is not a real kiss.

lxc_6fd5d6109b8c42d3.text: They keep the family names from their parents all their lives.

lxc_21c0a87bc5a099f5.text: The famous painter Pablo Picasso shows this.

lxc_d476c67e9207cf17.text: Most people in Spain have one first name and two family names.

lxc_f8fa86acce68a982.text: His two family names were Ruiz and Picasso.

lxc_ebfd27f1a155bcbc.text: So brothers and sisters always have the same two family names.

lxc_6133050e439af376.text: The first family name usually comes from the father.

lxc_2b86b9f74a051d0a.text: The second family name comes from the mother.

lxc_93d473d4307d15ad.text: Ruiz was his father's family name, and Picasso was his mother's.

lxc_c61baac39ebabbb3.text: Today, parents can choose which family name comes first.

lxc_eab61615ab12581f.text: Later, he used only his mother's name.

lxc_19622862029e03e6.text: But all the children in one family must have the same order.

lxc_6fdd558b2fd29177.text: So one name shows both sides of the family.

lxc_309a5cb7c7651d54.text: When women in Spain marry, they do not change their names.

lxc_bf5b9fbcf17d1772.text: Many are funny, because they make jokes about famous people and the news.

lxc_b90a72a064fcc4fb.text: At the end of winter, the days got longer, so they burned the old wood.

lxc_e1fa2cc207bcba8b.text: They did it on 19 March, the day of Saint Joseph.

lxc_3b708fa649aa7011.text: Saint Joseph also worked with wood, so he was special to them.

lxc_f107beb5d1d13bd0.text: The idea comes from carpenters, people who make things from wood.

lxc_817c48f5f06ab02a.text: Every March, the city of Valencia has a big festival called Las Fallas.

lxc_56cba1f29bc2e7b3.text: Fallas are made of wood and paper, and some are as tall as a building.

lxc_83f75acde5b98b2b.text: Every year, visitors vote for their favourite ninot.

lxc_ff050d779df18b29.text: This fire night is called la Cremà.

lxc_efc079b7e6574de7.text: In winter, they used old wood to hold candles, so they could work at night.

lxc_a7f135d7f21cb2c5.text: Each part of the city makes a falla.

lxc_99b0ef4a64c24397.text: A falla is a very big group of many figures.

lxc_120f2bcd3be4199f.text: The winners are saved from the fire and go to a museum.

lxc_1a45ade474190b8c.text: On the night of 19 March, people burn almost all of them.

lxc_fa78f2d97855c971.text: Each figure in a falla is a ninot.

lxc_cf9feb54512a4e3b.text: People call them the islands of eternal spring, a spring that never ends.

lxc_2fd65f76fd9662b8.text: The Canary Islands are seven big islands in the Atlantic Ocean.

lxc_cd3f4a79ebd3a7a7.text: They are part of Spain, but only about 100 kilometres from Africa.

lxc_3329f3377f1ce97a.text: The islands were made by volcanoes.

lxc_c701194030f319bc.text: So winter and summer are not very different.

lxc_0052f6c1e13d2164.text: The volcano Teide is on Tenerife, the biggest island.

lxc_83271d0b77f3c3a1.text: It is the highest mountain in Spain.

lxc_3e777f9509486b8b.text: The weather is warm all year, and it does not change much.

lxc_f66593e043859e6f.text: Winters are warm, because the islands are far south.

lxc_a031a2c0686ddba8.text: In summer, the sea is cool and the wind blows on most days.

lxc_65700658f3651a1b.text: So for more than a thousand years, pilgrims have walked there.

lxc_21206583ee3989f6.text: It is a long walk to the city of Santiago de Compostela.

lxc_9a1e7cddcff232b9.text: Camino de Santiago is Spanish for the Way of Saint James.

lxc_6c35f887f83f4dba.text: People on the Camino carry a pilgrim passport.

lxc_dc09e00d163ad5b1.text: The most popular way starts in France and is about 800 kilometres long.

lxc_d0ea89d02f14eae4.text: Saint James was one of the first people to follow Jesus.

lxc_c7c966e4e7e9d81f.text: That is why many people start in Sarria, just over 100 kilometres from Santiago.

lxc_4be04fba072599d6.text: To get it, pilgrims must walk at least the last 100 kilometres.

lxc_c0a139e3037d6414.text: The city is in the north-west of Spain.

lxc_ac817c82286c6761.text: At the end, pilgrims can get the Compostela.

lxc_20a44da31943c47e.text: People believe he is buried in the big church of the city.

lxc_fe6437b1154e494a.text: On this part, they need at least two stamps every day.

lxc_65ade5c2e1a2b008.text: Pilgrims are people who travel to a special church or place.

lxc_e799e106c3421f5a.text: It is a special paper with their name on it.

lxc_f37a6bdd13c2cae5.text: The stamps show where they walked.

lxc_85ce097bd45ce2c7.text: In each town where they sleep, they get a stamp in it.

lxc_fc6946745ad939c2.text: It is Spanish for over the table.

lxc_3caf74d50cc60e2d.text: It is a Sunday in March, a few days before Las Fallas.

lxc_ba989a9dcea8889f.text: Then make a plan for Las Fallas.

lxc_a22e35ae7be426aa.text: Your goal is to say hello and ask about names.

lxc_193c67b1cb786636.text: This time is called the sobremesa.

lxc_4c7ab5679f01e89f.text: Your friend Lucía invites you to lunch at her family's home in Valencia.

lxc_486c6dcd437c2104.text: In Spain, people often stay at the table after a meal and talk.

lxc_f357a9605c81d091.text: A very big falla stands in the City Hall Square.

lxc_b989b604442606f9.text: The streets are full of people.

lxc_577a5d76cf6a5504.text: Your goal is to ask when the fallas burn and why people burn them.

lxc_3c4c9379e5ea9626.text: You meet Lucía and Javier there.

lxc_59b7880cc7eeee9b.text: It is the night of 19 March.

lxc_39d345cd419c0ac1.text: Your goal is to get a bed and a pilgrim passport.

lxc_381089cb8f3c1e78.text: You go to a pilgrim hostel, a cheap place where pilgrims sleep.

lxc_0b790a12eb20df28.text: In summer, you arrive in Sarria to walk the last part of the Camino.

lxc_b6b58d45c71ffc0d.text: Choose one scene and act out the conversation.

lxc_705f805117111319.text: At the end, choose one Spanish custom and explain its reason to your partner.

lxc_13286a39d671b368.text: One of you is the visitor, and the other is Lucía, Carmen, Javier or Manuel.
